case_name: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
legal_principle: The procedure affecting life or personal liberty under Article 21 must be fair, just and reasonable, and not arbitrary.

case_name: Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India
legal_principle: The right to privacy is protected as a fundamental right under the Constitution, including through the protections of Article 21.

case_name: Lalita Kumari v. Government of U.P.
legal_principle: Registration of FIR is mandatory if the information discloses the commission of a cognizable offence, and no preliminary inquiry is permissible in such cases.

case_name: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar
legal_principle: Arrest should not be made routinely or merely because an offence is cognizable. Police officers must satisfy themselves about the necessity for arrest using objective criteria.

case_name: Arjun Panditrao Khotkar v. Kailash Kushanrao Gorantyal
legal_principle: Production of an electronic record certificate is mandatory for admitting secondary evidence of electronic records in court proceedings.

case_name: Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab
legal_principle: The extreme penalty of death for murder should only be imposed in the 'rarest of rare cases' when the alternative option of life imprisonment is unquestionably foreclosed.

case_name: Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia v. State of Punjab
legal_principle: Anticipatory bail under procedural criminal law is an integral component of personal liberty under Article 21; powers of the High Court and Sessions Court to grant it should not be circumscribed by unwarranted judge-made restrictions.
Maintenance is a social justice measure to prevent destitution; both parties must file comprehensive affidavits of disclosure of assets and liabilities to determine just and realistic quantum.

case_name: Social Action Forum for Manav Adhikar v. Union of India
legal_principle: The statutory provision dealing with cruelty by husband or relatives was enacted to combat marital cruelty; investigation and arrests must balance protection of victim with procedural fairness.
